items.title: Return a JSON 404 from StorageController.peek when the file is missing on disk
items.body:
## Problem
`bridge/apps/backend/src/storage/storage.controller.ts:130` calls `res.download(path, name)` with no error callback. The sibling `download` route (lines 79-99) handles the case where the DB row exists but the file is gone from disk (uploads/ does not survive a redeploy without a volume) and answers `404 {message:'File is missing on disk'}`. `peek` does not, so the client gets a bare Express error response. The Worker page's decrypt-before-job flow, which depends on `peek`, then cannot show a clear message. `storage.controller.spec.ts` has a `describe` for `download` only.

## Proposed change
Pass the same error callback to `res.download` in `peek`: log a warning, and if `!res.headersSent` send `404 {message:'File is missing on disk'}`. Do not delete the file. Extract a small private helper if it avoids duplicating the callback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `peek` responds 404 with `{message:'File is missing on disk'}` when `res.download` reports an error before headers are sent
- [ ] `peek` never calls `storageService.delete`
- [ ] New `peek` tests in `storage.controller.spec.ts` cover the success path and the missing-file path
- [ ] Existing `download` behaviour is unchanged and its tests pass

items.title: Guard ChatService.completeTurn/failTurn against non-pending assistant messages
items.body:
## Problem
`bridge/apps/backend/src/chat/chat.service.ts:166-190`: `completeTurn` and `failTurn` call `findOwnedMessage` (lines 149-164), which checks only ownership, then overwrite `content` and `status` unconditionally. A call with the id of a user message overwrites the user's text with assistant text. A late or duplicate worker report can flip a `Complete` message to `Failed`, or replace finished content.

## Proposed change
In both methods, throw `BadRequestException` or `ConflictException` unless `message.role === ChatMessageRole.Assistant` and `message.status === ChatMessageStatus.Running`. `claim()` (lines 111-122) is the only place that sets `Running`, so this matches the real flow. Add unit tests in `chat.service.spec.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `completeTurn` and `failTurn` reject a `User`-role message without saving
- [ ] They reject a message already `Complete` or `Failed` without saving
- [ ] They still succeed for a `Running` assistant message
- [ ] Tests cover all three cases for both methods

items.title: Keep `pull-issue --watch` polling after a transient error instead of exiting
items.body:
## Problem
`sync/src/commands/pullIssue.ts:113-120`: the `--watch` loop awaits `tryPullOnce` with no try/catch, so any network blip, bridge 5xx, or the dirty-tree check (lines ~26-31) rejects out of `pullIssueCommand` and ends the watch. That mode exists to wait unattended for a result, so it exits when it is needed. `gitlabWorker.ts:105-107` already catches errors in its equivalent loop, so the two watch loops are inconsistent.

## Proposed change
Wrap the `tryPullOnce` call in the loop in try/catch. On error, log a warning with the message and continue to the `sleep`. Keep the up-front `--watch` validation (lines 107-110) throwing. Extract the loop body or accept an injectable `pullOnce`/`sleep` so it can be tested.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A thrown error in one iteration is logged and the next iteration still runs
- [ ] The loop returns and notifies as before once `tryPullOnce` returns true
- [ ] Invalid `--watch` values still throw immediately
- [ ] A test in `sync/src/commands/` fails first with a rejecting then succeeding pull and passes afterwards

items.title: Make reports addOffDays/removeOffDay handle a year missing from props.json
items.body:
## Problem
`reports/packages/server/src/counts/props.ts`: `getProps` returns `undefined` for an absent year (line ~23), and `addOffDays` (line ~38) and `removeOffDay` (line ~73) dereference `yearProps.offDays` without a check. `importDayOffs` (line ~51) already defaults a missing year, so the three behave inconsistently. A POST or DELETE for a year not yet in `props.json` fails with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'offDays')`. `counts/handler.ts:38` also passes `req.body.dates` through without checking it is an array of date strings.

## Proposed change
In `addOffDays`, create the year entry with the same defaults `importDayOffs` uses. In `removeOffDay`, return without error if the year is absent. In `handler.ts`, reject a body whose `dates` is not an array of `YYYY-MM-DD` strings with a clear error event. Add tests against a temp props file.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `addOffDays` for an unknown year creates the year and stores the dates
- [ ] `removeOffDay` for an unknown year does not throw
- [ ] A missing or non-array `dates`, or a malformed date string, produces an error event and is not persisted
- [ ] Tests cover each case and the server test suite passes

items.title: Add an AbortSignal timeout to VpnService outbound fetch calls
items.body:
## Problem
`bridge/apps/backend/src/vpn/vpn.service.ts:78` and `:203` call `fetch` with no `AbortSignal`. A hung VPN panel or GitHub request holds the HTTP request open indefinitely and ties up a backend connection. The project already applies timeouts elsewhere: worker's fetches use `AbortSignal.timeout`, and `reports/packages/server/src/counts/handler.ts:108` does too.

## Proposed change
Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(<named constant, e.g. 10_000>)` to both `fetch` calls. Translate a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError` into the existing user-facing error path for an unreachable panel, for example a `BadGatewayException` with a clear message. Add a unit test that stubs `fetch` to reject with a `TimeoutError`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both fetch calls in `vpn.service.ts` carry a timeout signal
- [ ] A timeout surfaces as a clear 5xx-class error naming the panel/operation rather than an unhandled rejection
- [ ] A test covers the timeout path for each call
- [ ] Existing vpn tests pass
